source_review.notes: Checked twelve primary sources: original Misra-Gries, Karp-Shenker-Papadimitriou, Count-Min, Space-Saving, and bounded-deletion papers; current Apache DataSketches frequent-items documentation; current Apache Spark frequent-items, skew, and tuning documentation; and current Apache Flink adaptive-skew documentation/configuration/API. All URLs returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Reviewed true weight f_x, total N, heavy threshold phi, partition work w_j, absolute/relative thresholds T/gamma/m_0, Misra-Gries k, Count-Min epsilon/delta, salt count s_x, and candidate intervals.
Checked heavy hitter, top-k, candidate, exact verification, key skew, partition skew, straggler, and multidimensional work remain distinct.
Checked key/weight scope, snapshot/window, detector/hash/seed/version, summary attempt, skew generation, split ownership, replicated side, and output commit identities.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Frequency and execution work are not conflated; every threshold includes units, scope, and strictness.

evidence: Executed heavy-hitter-detection with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced median 15, maximum 120, factor 8, and a true dual-threshold flag.
Reproduced the 24-item Misra-Gries trace with candidates (hot,warm), threshold 6, and exact verified set (hot).
Recomputed Count-Min example width 2,719, depth 14, and one-million additive allowance for N=10^9 and epsilon=.001.
Recomputed exercises: 2,048/72=28.44; width 5,437, depth 12, 65,244 cells, 25,000 error; and six-billion join pairs with 40,000,000 replicated bytes.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable fixture validates one deterministic insertion-only summary trace and arithmetic only; it is not a weighted/deletion/merge proof, accuracy study, or distributed benchmark.

evidence: Verified dual skew predicate w_max>=T and w_max/max(m,m_0)>=gamma prevents negligible ratio-only triggers and zero denominators.
Reviewed Misra-Gries decrement accounting showing all items with f_x>N/k remain candidates with at most k-1 counters.
Checked standard Count-Min w=ceil(e/epsilon), d=ceil(ln(1/delta)), one-sided insertion error, and point-query confidence assumptions.
Verified aggregation salting by disjoint input ownership and one-sided join splitting via A_x times B_x as the disjoint union of A_x,i times B_x.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Detector guarantees do not prove runtime benefit, and join/aggregation split proofs do not transfer to arbitrary group functions.

evidence: Reviewed empty/all-empty partitions, zero median, tiny high ratios, threshold equality, ties, one/all heavy keys, many candidates, high cardinality, and rapidly changing distributions.
Reviewed row/byte/compute/state/output/placement skew, giant rows/groups, poor/adversarial hashes, counter overflow, weak seeds, deletions, weights, and many-query confidence.

Reviewed inner/outer/semi/anti splits, independent salting, replicated preserved rows, non-decomposable UDFs, output explosion, memory/disk/network/task limits, retry, speculation, and mixed generations.
Reviewed raw/digested-key inference, cross-tenant/region exposure, auth failure, telemetry cardinality, evidence expiry, holds, and deletion.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Detection accuracy, causal diagnosis, semantic coverage, operational benefit, failure safety, and privacy can fail independently.

evidence: Traced exact or approximate observations through complete accepted detector merge, candidate interval, optional exact verification, immutable skew plan, owned splits, and committed result.
Checked detector dimensions/hash/seeds/error model and key/weight/snapshot semantics remain compatible across distributed summaries.
Checked every aggregation input, join pair, and outer unmatched row has exactly one semantic output owner after mitigation.
Checked detector, summary, replication, salt/task, state, memory, disk, network, output, attempt, telemetry, and cleanup resources are bounded.
invariant_checking.notes: Slow-task causality must be established from resource evidence; frequency alone does not authorize a remediation.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from scoped work definition through causal evidence, detector selection/merge, verification, operator decomposition, plan ownership, admission, differential tests, and deletion.
Checked Misra-Gries candidate inclusion, Count-Min conditional point-error claim, aggregation salting, and one-sided join coverage.
Checked outer joins add unmatched ownership and arbitrary group functions may remain indivisible.

Reviewed counterexamples for mean-only diagnosis, ratio-only triggers, good-hash hot-key claims, ordinary repartitioning, sketch exactness, naive summary union, naive two-side salting, and speculation.
proof_review.notes: Algorithmic guarantees, operator correctness, and measured tail improvement are separate proof/evidence layers.

evidence: Audited uses of exact, candidate, verified, approximate, upper/lower bound, false positive/negative, confidence, insertion-only, nonnegative, independent, deterministic, supported, and safe.
Confirmed Count-Min and Misra-Gries claims state parameter, update-model, threshold, and verification conditions.
Confirmed Spark/Flink/DataSketches behavior is current and sourced, while algorithm papers support general claims.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No sample, sketch, stale statistic, or runtime threshold is mislabeled as universal exact truth.

evidence: Reviewed proposed measures for rows/bytes/CPU/state/spill/network/output/duration, quantiles/maxima/top share, detector parameters/errors, candidate verification, replication, tasks, and before/after tails.
Confirmed no universal skew factor, absolute threshold, sample rate, sketch size, hash, salt count, hot-key cap, split orientation, resource class, or retention period is prescribed.
Checked data versus infrastructure causes, frequency versus cost, estimated versus exact, mean versus tail, and mitigation benefit versus overhead remain separate.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production choices require representative distributions, operator semantics, resource topology, service objectives, failure/threat models, and policy evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed skew as multidimensional execution imbalance and heavy hitters as scoped frequency/weight properties, spanning robust metrics, exact/sample/summary/sketch detection, error contracts, verification, operator-specific splitting, adaptive plans, retries, security, and lifecycle.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed practical causal tracing, dual thresholds, detector merges, exact gray-zone verification, aggregation salting, join replication/outer ownership, indivisible groups, adaptive generations, admission, fault injection, protected telemetry, and expiry. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from skew definitions and diagnosis through detector algorithms, semantic mitigation, adaptive operation, validation, and governance. Ten examples and five complete exercises cover robust ratios, negligible skew, metric differences, sketch sizing, candidate guarantees, salted aggregation, join coverage, outer duplication, runtime control, and privacy.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark, Flink, or DataSketches maintainer, streaming-algorithms/statistics researcher, database/query-optimization specialist, runtime/network/storage/performance engineer, adversarial-security or privacy specialist, legal/records authority, affected-tenant reviewer, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
